title: Undiagnosed
body:
At the age of 42, I begun to realise that there’s a 99% chance that I have ADHD and am on the wait list to see a psych - who knows how long that will be. 

Whilst I don’t have a diagnosis, I can honestly relate to practically every that Rox shares, from not replying (or even opening) text messages, forgetting to shower, picking my clothes out of the floordrobe or washing the same load 5 times because I forget to hang it out. 

In my own research on ADHD, before I stumbled upon ADHD Love I had read about body doubling and how it can be useful to get things done. Reflecting back on my own behaviours, I realise that I definitely find it easier to do these mundane tasks when I have someone else around… so when you live alone, where does that get you? 

At first I was skeptical that the app would motivate me, but it is amazing how much it has helped and changed my routine. This morning I found myself tidying up my lounge before the app even reminded me. 

The only thing I would love to change is reminder function. It would be so much easier if could set the next time you did something by selecting a date or time, rather than adjusting it in hourly increments.

title: Worth It
body:
After humming and hawing for about a year on whether I should try this app I finally downloaded it. I checked out a guided task First and enjoyed editing my videos along side Rox and’s Rich. I figured I wanted to try the lives so I bought a month worth since it’s only $7 CAD or something like that and if I don’t enjoy it at least it’s not too much money but it’s still investing in my mental health.
Dubbii is different from other productivity apps because it’s a community of people with the goal of completing tasks. The lives are guided by hosts who keep the community safe and on task. With consent they will offer count downs for folks who ask and need an extra boost off the couch. The lives have a pomodoro timer and/or power hour that the hosts call out for those who enjoy that structure but you don’t have to follow that if you don’t want to. 
Each host has their own energy so if you don’t vibe with the first live you join don’t give up and try another. 
It was a bit confusing for me at first but I kept to it and I’ve got so much work done that I have time for myself in the evenings where I can do what I want guilt free!
The best part is Rox and Rich are neurodivergent themselves and they built the app with the community in mind and with their input as well. They find the apps that make it difficult to cancel predatory on neurodivergent minds so if you don’t find it useful it is easy to cancel your subscription. 
Might as well check it out, I would suggest giving Dubbii a chance because this app has been life changing for me and so many others. What have you got to lose?

author: Barnaby crumble

title: LIFE CHANGING
body:
Okay HOW does this work so well?! My mind is blown. Joined my first live yesterday and managed to get a whole pile of (very important) admin completed that I’d been putting off for SIX MONTHS. I feel so much lighter. Even if I never used it again, it was worth the annual subscription fee for that alone. (Although I will definitely be using this thing daily!!). Really enjoying the motivation from the lovely coaches, and also the focus rooms are awesome. I can see myself scheduling my day / certain tasks around lives going fwd. I felt a bit awkward at first putting my camera on, but it’s definitely more effective when you know you’re on show. There’s also something really nice about seeing other humans just doing ordinary human things. Laundry, washing dishes, admin, all the awesome and varied creative projects people do. I very quickly realised this was a judgement free zone and feel safe in this community.

I think Rox and Rich have created something truly extraordinary here. My absolute favourite thing about it is actually the follow-along videos. The fact they’re filmed in a normal home, not some manicured insta-worthy apartment, filmed on a phone in such a DIY, raw, unfiltered way is really where the magic is. The rest of the UX of the app is seamless and the layout is really clean and simple (not overstimulating at all and you can pick up how to use it in minutes). But the morning routing videos really got me. I even shed a little tear and laughed while following along. What an amazing way to help remove the shame that so many people with neurodivergence and trauma feel when struggling to get things done. 

Cannot recommend enough 💪

title: 5 stars 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
body:
I genuinely love the Dubbii app — it’s become one of my favorite apps to use daily. Everything about it feels well-designed and intentional, from how smooth the interface is to how well all the features actually work in real life. It’s incredibly easy to use, but still powerful, which is a hard balance to get right. Nothing feels confusing or cluttered, and everything just flows naturally, which makes staying organized and productive feel effortless instead of stressful.

The app runs really well with no bugs or lag, and it’s clear that a lot of thought went into making sure the user experience is actually enjoyable. It doesn’t feel like just another generic productivity app — it feels personal, motivating, and genuinely helpful. It’s one of those apps that you don’t just download and forget about, but actually keep using because it makes a real difference.

The only feature I would absolutely love to see added is a desk organization option. Something that helps with organizing physical desk setups, planning workspace layouts, or tracking desk organization ideas would be such an amazing addition. It would fit perfectly with the rest of the app’s purpose and vibe, and it would make it even more complete as an all-in-one organization and productivity tool.

Overall, Dubbii is an amazing app that clearly had a lot of care put into it, and I would 100% recommend it to anyone looking for a genuinely helpful, well-functioning, and enjoyable app. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

title: Best App for my ADHD (after trying others like Fabulous & Chillio which didn’t help)
body: This app is brilliant for three reasons: 1. Lived experience 2. Fun. 3. Community.  1. The developers have experience in dealing with ADHD, Autism, both in themselves and family. Therefore the videos are fit for purpose, and based on tried and tested methods, and are incredibly practical for getting the day to day, done. 2. Fun. The videos are an appropriate length, each task is divided into steps. They strike the right tone: a balance of fun but also authentic and they’ve included variations for different situations and moods. Their badge reward system measures progress, and doesn’t regress, just updates when you want to.  3. The live sessions are brilliant for when you’ve run out of energy and motivation. It helps to make your ‘To Dos’ became ‘Tah Dahs!’ Each session has a host who encourages action, empathises a little with blocks, cheers successes, and celebrates the community. ‘Dubbers’ in the chat, have the opportunity not only to share, but to cheer, send hugs, give reminders and generally give each other a boost of energy ‘Dubbii Dust’ and a sense of togetherness.  All this for just under £30 a year, which suits the budgets of students, people with limited income during this time of inflation. As I’m from a teaching background, I think this is one of the best things to come out of the online-universe - helping students to complete tasks, and helping people long undiagnosed, find some kind of support, as they sit on waiting lists, or wait to have enough money to pay for treatment and medication.  This app deserves to be given the Apple App of the year award… I think it’s amazing. My house is clean, my things are being organised, my body is cared for, and my long-shelved projects are getting attention again. It’s has added such value to my life, i hope it lasts for decades - and never compromises on its down-to-earth, accessibility.  Bravo Rox & Rich.

title: Perfect for anyone struggling with their Mental or Physical Health
body:
This app is life changing. At 35 years old with possible adhd/autism and a partner with likely autism, I've always struggled with time anxiety, procrastination, either clock watching or time blindness which makes me overwhelmed. I've got a pile of journals with to do lists and planners in effort to get organised and build up habits every adult should have but nothing stuck long term.

With this app, before I know it I've started a quick bed time routine, a morning routine. We have our laundry from the week put away. The key is not trying to be perfect and follow the clips you're interested in most at that time, and then set the nudge for next time. It sets it either for tomorrow for the daily things or the week for the weekly things which is great. 

Mondays, used to feel overwhelming, hunting for clean clothes or sleeping in too late for a shower before work. This morning I've had my shower in a clean bathroom. Our bedroom is tidy (did it yesterday!) I've now had my coffee and a glass of water and will have some breakfast and still have an hour to kill before work. Is this how it's supposed to be?! Followed you both for awhile and this app is like the cherry on the cake of content. Super grateful to you both. ❤️❤️❤️

title: More than an app, a community 💛
body:
I joined Dubbii after coming across one of their Facebook videos. It looked so warm and inviting that I just had to give it a try.

I've had an ADHD diagnosis for 15 years, yet Dubbii has helped me understand myself better than ever before. The videos have taught me practical ways to approach everyday household tasks, and the live sessions have become a safe and supportive part of my daily life.

From the very beginning, I felt incredibly welcome. The hosts are kind, knowledgeable and genuinely passionate about what they do, and the community is full of people who understand each other without judgement. There is absolutely no pressure or shame. Whether you're having an amazing day, struggling to get started, or only manage one tiny task, you're met with kindness and encouragement.

One of my favourite things is that there's a live body doubling session every three hours, 24/7, with each session lasting an hour. It gives my days structure, keeps me motivated, and means I never have to wait long for the next session if I need a little extra support.

I wholeheartedly recommend Dubbii to anyone who struggles with everyday life, whether you have ADHD or simply need a little extra motivation, structure and support. Dubbii has genuinely changed my life. It has helped me understand myself better, trust myself more, and create more structure in my daily life. 

I can honestly say that subscribing to Dubbii has been one of the best decisions I've made for myself. 💛

So… I’m hoping very much at the developers will see this and take steps to make their app accessible for blind users like myself. Please test your app with mobile device screen readers like Apple‘s built-in voiceover so that I can use it. If you do that, I will happily change this review to five stars and absolutely gush about it. This is a cry for help, not an attempt to tear this thing down. author: Pharagill

title: The ADHD App that WORKS
body:
Just coming in for a thankful moment! 

TL:DR: Dubbi has been so helpful, and has helped me with internal self talk more than I thought anything possibly could. 

My Experience so far: 

After lurking for a while watching Rox and Ricky on Youtube, I found myself back in ADHD burn out or closely approaching it. I started therapy and slowly the weight fell off, and unfortunately as we unpacked while building coping skills I felt that weight build back up. We were at a point where scheduled vacation turned into a longer vacation and sick time because daily panic attacks for hours are not friendly to anyone, and even less so to connective tissue disorder folx. 

So at the same time my homework was to “Be Kind to Yourself”, I found Dubbii. At first, the external structure was a support in itself as I tried to figure out if this would work for me. Then it turned into peaceful anchors to my day, and slowly my internal scripts started rewriting themselves. The “author experience” of this process is still underway but is honestly more improved than I could have hoped for. Now after over a month or so of the sessions my own voice kindly reminds me to care and “be nicer to myself and others”. Instead of doom spiraling, Mariah’s Coconut Mall starts to play, and the anxious thoughts get noticed with Nicki’s “Oh I hope you are okay, we are here for you” with my own kind of spin to it. More noticeably two very mild panics attacks in that timeframe, down from daily when starting. In 6 weeks! 

On top of this, doom piles were cleaned, cabinets organized, work was more manageable, I gained more of a sense of community, and feel better. While there’s still work to be done, “thats okay we are gonna roll it over to the next day” and it’s more doable with Dubbii. 

While medication and professional help cannot replace Dubbii, it IS an amazing add on to the full self care toolbox. Both my therapist and psychiatry providers have it as a shareable option now with their clients after my experience and I am so glad this exists. 

Thank you! And see ya at the next session!

title: Great for body doubling
body: This is a great app for body doubling. You can use the videos where they take you step-by-step through tasks like how to make a bed, etc.,   You can also use the live one hour Zoom sessions. This is where you have one coordinator Who reads chat messages and respond to us. There are also a whole bunch of people doing things on camera and you can choose to body double with each other. But you don’t have to get on camera if you don’t want to. The organizers are very responsive to the needs of the community. I live in the US and they started with sessions that were centered around UK daytimes. But they have some more sessions and I can attend the 3pm (my time) one. It is a pretty new app and they are still evolving. I suggest everyone try this and see if it works for them.
author: RJ yes another one

title: A lot better than you think
body:
I heard about the app from social media videos. At first I had my doubts - a lot of the videos go by really quickly and it almost looked like, at first, a lot of the tasks that were being taken on were not as overwhelming as the ones I was struggling with. I felt very ashamed and was wondering if this was not for me. Let alone, the live body doubling sessions could be overwhelming at times. 

 Then I realized - in the prerecorded videos - Roxanne and Rich deal with different workloads that are appropriate for neurotypical and neurodivergent people. A great example of this is their de cluttering videos. While Roxanne deals with an overwhelming closet / wash room, Rich is dealing with a larger room. I was feeling a lot less ashamed - they are dealing with the same amount of struggle but Roxanne is trying to balance something more manageable. 

 The messy mode videos are the ones that struck home with being the most relatable and had me feeling the most comfortable. Rather than individual steps or a short body doubling video, these are your long videos with some sections you can jump between. Seeing the mess helped me feel a lot less ashamed because it was what I was dealing with at the time. The step by step instructions were great. 

 One of the ideal videos I like with a timer is the study time one. I love that it has background noise and it’s working in complete silence otherwise. I wish we had more videos like that. I still think that some of the timed videos are a little too fast for me - I work best without shorter timers. And the live body doubling gets a lot to get used to - because I feel like I have to respond or be on camera. But honestly - if you say nothing and keep it in the background it works really well. 

 Plus - since they’re based in the UK - there’s a lot here for those of us who use other body doubling that only has morning or afternoon slots. This allows a lot of great work to be done for night owls in the US. Overall, if you are looking for a rather cheap subscription app that works decently for body doubling and background noise - this is very solid. 

I use it on top of another ADHD app for coaching / body doubling. It will not replace a coach - but those coaching sessions are expensive and this gets you by.

Update: The only suggestions I would have is being able to register with another email so that I can switch between my Android phone and iPad without having to pay a subscription twice. Plus, I would love a website version! Looking forward to seeing any new body doubling videos I saw from Developer replies, and more fun things with body doubling. 

Thank you for a wonderful new community to be part of and helping us feel not ashamed - and proud of how much we’ve accomplished!

title: This is a LIFE SAVING app!!!
body:
You guys are absolutely incredible. I've been using dubbii for several months now and the way it has entirely changed my headspace when it comes to doing necessary (but often not fun) tasks is remarkable. 

Firstly, it's like having someone there with you doing the task. As someone who lives alone, this has had such a positive impact. I'm often embarrassed at how messy my space can become when I don't have the bandwidth to stay on top of things, so the prospect of inviting a friend over to body double while I clean is a vulnerable, intimidating thing. With dubbii, there's zero fear of judgement. 

Additionally, each task is marked with a time estimate. I didn't realise how helpful this was until a few months in, but part of my dread of starting tasks has to do with the amount of time I *think* it's going to take in my head. When I see that the washing up is only going to take 10-20 minutes, I don't drag my feet to start. It seems like a surmountable task.

Another thing I love is the ability to choose who to follow along with. Roxy's videos are always fun and full of energy, while Rich's videos are very calming and methodical, so you can choose based on your own personality or current mood/vibe. They both have a way of making you feel unjudged, while proving that each task is really not as big and scary as your brain has made it out to be.

The option to choose just a simple body doubling video with no instructions (for those times when you don't want to be told what to do) or a step by step guide to the task (for the times when you don't have enough spoons to remember what comes next) is also *majorly* helpful. 

They have a "make a suggestion" button at the bottom of the task video list. I suggested a packing tutorial a few months ago and took a short break from using the app, and I see now they've made videos for packing! Whether it was my suggestion they took, multiple of the same suggestion, or something they'd already planned to do, it seems like they have new tasks and features coming out consistently, and I love that they are interested in listening to what the users want/need.

Thank you so so much for this app guys!! 🖤✨

title: Dubbii is SO SMART!!😃
body: I have been using dubbii for a while and I really think that this is the best thing for me. Sometimes it takes me all day to make the bed and then when I finally do make the bed it’s time to go to bed, and then I never feel accomplished. I would rate this app 10 out of 10 stars. body: I have only just begun to use this app and I am loving it. Like for cleaning if there is a definitely do this to avoid mold, nasty smells etc to other times when i want to clean out my fridge. i think it would be fun if deeper cleaning things were suggested as bonus items and get points for doing them. it would make them feel less like a chore. it would also be cool if there was a note taking portion of the app to store thoughts about chores or tasks but you don’t necessarily want to be a nudge. I was also thinking about if there was a way for users to create custom tasks that let’s say i have a specific task to do, i could break down the steps and have it stored in the app as a task i could complete many times over, yea it wouldn’t have the body doubling portion but i think it would be useful itself. i think a fun thing to add to the body doubling portion is if it showed you how many people had that task open , don’t have to show who it is (although if you had friends on it and could see what one of your friends was working on or struggling on and sending a message or some interactive feature). thinking about if there is a way for when i first grab my phone in the morning it would open the morning routine (or another task) making me more inclined to go ahead and get up and do it. i know this is a lot but it’s been making me think a lot about how we can use social media to our advantage instead of doom scrolling all the time.  even if only one of these things happened i’d be so happy. some im sure are more complicated than others and ive never built an app but just an excited adhd person wanting to get everything i can out of an amazing app.

title: Breath of air
body:
Hopefully an example that will land for the folks that are debating using this app. 

I grew up in a relatively day-to-day unsteady environment when most kids would be learning consistency for cleaning their room or developing good hygiene habits, etc. I didn’t get that. I knew brushing my teeth was necessary but ya just throw the toothpaste on a brush and call it good, right? Nope, ya gotta floss, and brush, and use mouthwash; at least that’s what was always preached but never taught to me. To some this may seem stupidly simple but it wasn’t and as I got older the potential embarrassment grew, how can I be in my late teens then early twenties then late twenties without having a routine for brushing my teeth?

I’ve never had an “easy” time at the dentist and I always dreaded it every time because it was painful but I had to deal with it. After using this app and getting off to a running start with the teeth brushing video, I may not brush my teeth every night but I. Have. A. Routine. I now know how it feels to have my teeth and mouth clean on a daily basis. And ya know what? Not 4 months brushing my teeth like I learned with the app and I had the EASIEST dental cleaning in my life! As it turns out, doing those things regularly and accurately makes the preventative appointments so much better. I walked out of the building feeling accomplished and so ‘adult’ and now brushing my teeth is a habit I have always wanted and never had. Without this app, I don’t know if that would have been as possible. 

To anyone debating, give it a shot. Try the free videos and you’ll know whether you want it or not, I will say it has been an absolute saving grace.

title: Missing the point
body:
A video tutorial maybe? But this is not body doubling. Who ever made these videos is kind of missing the point of body doubling. The videos are short, with the steps described rather than acted out for a lot of them. These videos are SHORT, like 15 seconds. You cannot watch these videos while doing the tasks at all. 

I started with room clean, their room is spotless, only like 2 cups and a small piece of trash. So naturally it takes her 20 seconds to pick up all trash. This is completely unrealistic for 90% of ND individuals. The whole point of the word ‘doubling’ implies we are doing the same thing at the same time. This is just a paid video of someone saying ‘pick up your trash’ and then you having to do it on your own. Don’t bother.

title: Validation: showers are exhausting
body:
I thought I was the only one that hated showers but took them as often as I could force my self.  Sure, taking out the trash and room of doom is awesome and I have definitely used those videos.  But the one that I keep coming back to is the shower.  When I heard Rox say ‘so much effort showering’ (for the first time), I thought ‘I’m not the only one!   

Other things I like: 
There are two styles of doubling. I tend towards Rox, because she has ADHD and reminds us of things that I seem to always forget (get the towel and put on deodorant). Rich is also great. 
I love that I feel like they are having conversations with me as they go along. (Except in the shower, that’s quiet). 
I love the celebration at the end and the badges. 

Also, as a plug for their content, they explain things so well.  I feel like Rox explains it the way I’m thinking, then Rich explains it how I would like to but can’t articulate it to non-ADHDers.  And I thank you! This late diagnosis adhd mom with her adhd son loves you all the way from the US in South Carolina! 

Thank you for taking a chance and opening up!!!

title: Love the Concept, need Larger Screen Capabilities
body: I’ve just opened the app (after having downloaded it a month ago and then forgetting I had it) and so far I love the concept and 90% of the execution. But where there’s a huge disconnect for me is that when I, say, call a friend to body double they’ll usually talk to me while I complete a task, and so while my brain is occupied in listening and trying to answer a conversation my body is able to take care of tasks. I get this isn’t practical for the app, but then I miss out on the other part of body doubling which is having someone in the room with you. The body doubling screen is so brilliant, but so small — I find myself needing to hold my phone to trick my brain, but then I just end up doom scrolling. An app for a smart TV might be too big of an ask, but a way to “cast” or “stream” the body doubling footage to my TV would be so helpful because as Rox works, I can work. Anyways — I really recommend anyone to just try the app out once, my problems might not be the same as yours, and the concept is so, so cool. Thank you!

I was wondering if in the future you might include something to help breakdown larger, less specific tasks? Or just have a random body double for whatever we might need it for? I’m talking like reorganizing the closet in the hall or tackling the (very scary) basement/attic storage. Or cooking dinner or exercising. Because some tasks are harder for you to break down for us or they’re unique to a person but it would still be helpful to not have to do them alone. Like you could offer words of encouragement or take breaks with us and still help us stay motivated? Also any tips for making a routine/schedule? Breaking down how to make a monthly calendar? Just a few ideas! I hope it’s helpful! And I REALLY look forward to the self-care update! I’m so excited to sign up as soon as I can! Thank you!
